rules.config_choice: Compare A and B on val_eval only (KrunBench validation + val_hard + val_tools). Primary: mean of intent core accuracy (KrunBench val) and tool core accuracy (val_tools). Choose B only if it beats A by >= 0.5 pp on that mean; otherwise the cheaper A. Ties within 0.5 pp -> A.
rules.abstention_score: Among the three scores (after per-family temperature), choose the one with the highest mean OOD AUROC over {KrunBench val intents, val_tools} on val_eval; if within 0.005, the lower mean AURC wins.
rules.final_report: holdout_tools and KrunBench v0 test (incl. BFCL) are evaluated once for Laya and the chosen Krun One after the choices above are frozen in results/krun_one_decisions.json; nothing is tuned afterwards.

note: all choices made on validation val_eval only; this file unlocks the final sets (holdout_tools, kb_test), evaluated once

v0_1.reason: No single clear, data-fixable failure. Config B errors on val_eval: intent 4.4% (kb_val), hard 8.7%, tools 5.1%; largest residual = near-OOD (gold label removed) false acceptance ~8-10% at the 0.98 operating point, and inspection shows most accepted options are legitimately close/interchangeable labels (card_arrival<->card_delivery_estimate, failed_transfer<->declined_transfer, calendar_set<->calendar_query, general_quirky catch-all) — label ambiguity of the near-OOD construction, not a model gap. Other residuals (32-option intents 13%, unseen tools 7.1% vs 3.0% seen, pt/es +1-3 pp) are moderate and spread, so an error-mined second round would be a tuning loop, which the sprint rules exclude.
